lines.text: Your best friends sent hearts. The gym guy sent the job.
Rewind. You had the best crew alive. Ride or die since high school.
You tell the group chat. Hearts. Prayers. Zero leads.
Three months. Two hundred applications. Nothing.
Then a guy from the gym. You've talked twice. He sends you a link.
Two weeks later, you're hired. More money than before.
Your boys know the same people you know. They hear about the same jobs.
The guy you barely know lives in a different world. He sees doors you can't.
A study of 282 workers. The ones hired through a contact? Only one in six saw that person often.
lines.say: A study of two hundred eighty two workers. The ones hired through a contact? Only one in six saw that person often.

lines.text: LinkedIn tested twenty million people. The best ties for a new job? Not distant contacts. Not best friends. The people in between.
So keep your boys. But text the guy from the gym.
Strong ties produce belonging. Weak ties produce mobility.
